title: Four laws and their opposites
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which of the four laws are you using on your team?
I summarized: to create good habits, make it obvious, make it attractive, make it easy and make it satisfying.
To break bad habits, I said, invert them: make it invisible, make it unattractive, make it difficult and make it unsatisfying.

I said that as a leader you do an inventory: how am I going to make it obvious, attractive and easy for someone to pick up the phone and make forty calls? How is it a symbol of a higher calling and not just simple tasks?
I asked: what is the personal symbol, and what is invested in your name?
Pick one task your team avoids. How would you make it obvious, attractive, easy and satisfying?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a good habit you want from your team.
Write how to make it obvious.
Write how to make it attractive, easy and satisfying.
Write a bad habit to break and how to make it invisible and hard.
Write the higher calling behind the task.

check.q: What are the four laws for good habits, as I summarized?
How do you break a bad habit, according to my summary?
What did I say a leader does?
choices: An inventory of how to make it obvious, attractive and easy

recap: Use the four laws. Invert them for bad habits. Take an inventory as a leader.
